sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax for a Tampa home?
sections.html:
Tampa sits in Hillsborough County, so the county property appraiser values your home and the county tax collector sends and collects the bill. The City of Tampa is one of the taxing authorities on that bill and sets only its own millage. The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's main office is in the County Center at 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard, 15th Floor, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday to Friday, phone 813-272-6100.

The Tax Collector's office handles payments at 813-635-5200 and through HillsTaxFL.gov, with drop boxes and service centers. For questions about a millage rate or a taxing authority's budget, the collector's office tells owners to contact that authority directly, using the contact details printed on the bill.

sections.h2: What is the City of Tampa millage rate?
sections.html:
Tampa City Council adopted a rate of 6.2076 mills for fiscal year 2026 through Resolution 2025-813, passed 6 to 0 at the council meeting. The resolution levies that rate on all real and personal taxable property in the city. A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of taxable value, and the city's rate sits beside county, school and special district lines on your notice.

The Property Appraiser publishes final millage sheets each year comparing the City of Tampa, Temple Terrace, Plant City and unincorporated Hillsborough County, and the 2026 sheet is posted on its Truth in Millage page. Each column covers one taxing area, so use the column that matches your parcel. Rates for later fiscal years are set by new council resolutions, so confirm the current figure with the tax office.

sections.h2: When are Tampa property taxes due and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Hillsborough County property tax bills for the 2026 roll opened for collection on November 1, 2026, and all of that year's taxes are due by March 31, 2027. The Tax Collector mailed nearly 515,000 notices on October 30, 2026 and expects to collect about $4.1 billion across the county.

The same pattern repeats each year: bills in November, discounts that shrink monthly, and delinquency after the March deadline. Florida law makes unpaid taxes delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Tampa assessment or claim an exemption?
sections.html:
The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser sends the annual TRIM notice to every owner no later than the end of August, showing the estimated just value as of January 1. If you disagree with the value, Florida's revenue department says to file a petition with the value adjustment board through the clerk within 25 days of the notice of proposed property taxes. Denied exemptions have a separate 30 day window after the denial letter was mailed.

  • Exemption and classification applications are due March 1.
  • Tangible personal property returns for business owners are due April 1.
  • The homestead is available only where the owner lives in the home as a permanent resident on January 1.

Call the Property Appraiser at 813-272-6100 before the deadline if your notice looks wrong. A rental owner should also remember that renting a homesteaded home can end the exemption.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the tax on a Tampa house?
sections.html:
A sale resets the assessment, so the buyer's bill can be well above yours. The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser explains that a homestead home is capped at 3% growth a year, but the capped value stays in effect only for the year of purchase, then the home is reassessed at market value. You may pay a pro-rated share of the seller's taxes at closing, yet the following year's assessment reflects the new market value.

State materials set the cap at the lower of 3% or the CPI change, and the sale counts as a change of ownership that resets the property on the next January 1. Buyers who ask what the seller pays are looking at a figure that will not carry over.

  • Seller's homestead ends when the home stops being the permanent residence.
  • Portability lets a seller who buys another Florida home carry over part of the saved value, when the new homestead is established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was given up.
  • The claim uses Form DR-501T filed with the new homestead application by March 1.

sections.h2: What do Tampa's neighborhoods and history mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Tampa's older areas were built in distinct waves, and age and location shape what buyers ask about. The city's history page says Fort Brooke was established in 1824, Henry B. Plant's railroad extension reached the Hillsborough River in 1884, and phosphate shipping and the 1886 cigar factory of Vicente Martinez Ybor shaped growth. Ybor City covers about two square miles between Nebraska Avenue, 22nd Street, Columbus Drive and East Broadway.

A building boom from 1923 to 1926 produced many subdivisions, including Davis Island, a man-made island at the mouth of the Hillsborough River built by D.P. Davis. Today, MacDill Air Force Base houses U.S. Central Command and U.S. Special Operations Command, and the city's port is described as the seventh largest in the nation.

For a seller, older homes often mean questions about repairs and permits. Ask the City of Tampa about permits and any historic district rules before you start work.

sections.h2: What does Florida charge at closing on a Tampa house?
sections.html:
Florida's deed tax is a documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk of court when the deed is recorded. Every party to the document is liable by statute, whichever side agrees to pay. Miami-Dade has a different rate, so the Hillsborough rate is the standard one.

  • Order a payoff for any unpaid tax year from the Tax Collector.
  • Ask the closing agent to prorate the current year's tax.
  • Keep a copy of the closing statement for your records.

Taxes that stay unpaid can reach a tax certificate sale. The certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years, so clear delinquent years before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Can I sell my Tampa house if property taxes are behind?
sections.html:
Yes, but the unpaid tax must be satisfied at closing, usually from your proceeds. Get a payoff from the Hillsborough County Tax Collector and add it to any mortgage payoff when you weigh an offer. A buyer who purchases as is can close without repairs, which helps when funds are tight.

Compare a direct sale against listing, considering commissions, repairs, months of carrying cost and how much delinquent tax accrues in the meantime.

faqs.q: What is the City of Tampa's property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City Council adopted 6.2076 mills for fiscal year 2026 by Resolution 2025-813. That is only the city portion, and your bill also lists county, school and other taxing authorities.

faqs.q: When are Tampa property taxes due?
faqs.a: Hillsborough bills for the 2026 roll are due by March 31, 2027. Pay by November 30, 2026 for 4%, December 31 for 3%, January 31 for 2% and February 28 for 1%.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Tampa property value or exemptions?
faqs.a: Call the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser at 813-272-6100. Questions about payments go to the Tax Collector at 813-635-5200.

faqs.q: Does the homestead cap carry over to the buyer in Tampa?
faqs.a: No. The Property Appraiser says the capped value remains only for the year of purchase, and then the home is reassessed at market value.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Tampa deed?
faqs.a: All parties to the document are liable under state rules, whichever side agrees to pay. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected at recording.
